column1: photography|Choose informative optics, realistic exposure, focus and physically motivated light; preserve actual surface behavior.
illustration|Use authored silhouette, contour and shape hierarchy; detail should communicate the supplied idea rather than imitate a photograph.
painting|Specify pigment deposition, edge variation and support appropriate to the selected medium; retain focal structure beneath brushwork.
drawing|Describe stroke direction, pressure, line weight and tonal construction; avoid incompatible painted gloss.
printmaking|Use the chosen matrix, ink and registration logic; distinguish carved, etched, stamped and screened marks.
3d-cgi|Keep modeled topology, contact, scale and material parameters coherent under one camera and lighting arrangement.
product|Preserve exact silhouette, components, supplied branding and finish; reflections should reveal construction rather than distort it.
architecture|Maintain structural support, repeated module scale, openings, ground contact and coherent projection.
interior|Preserve room layout and circulation; align furniture scale, wall junctions and window/interior exposure.
landscape|Organize landform continuity, horizon and distance planes; do not invent terrain features absent from the brief.
poster|Prioritize supplied message, focal image, margins and hierarchy; reserve exact text space only when text is requested.
advertisement|Make the supplied product or claim clear without inventing promises, statistics, branding or endorsements.
logo|Prioritize distinctive simple geometry, legibility and scalable negative space; use only supplied lettering and avoid unrelated brand marks.
icon|Design a compact recognizable silhouette with consistent stroke or fill grammar and enough internal spacing at small size.
diagram|Show supplied parts and relationships with clear endpoints and consistent notation; do not invent technical facts.
infographic|Keep data and relationships exact, use consistent scale and encoding, and avoid fabricated statistics or labels.
map|Preserve topology, route connections, supplied names and orientation; simplify metric detail only when the brief permits.
abstract|Make the chosen process, shape relationship or material behavior observable without inventing literal narrative objects.
material-study|Isolate the requested material's roughness, transmission, reflection and surface scale while preserving object geometry.
multi-subject-action|Enumerate subjects and attributes, clarify ownership and contact, separate silhouettes, and prevent unintended extra subjects or fused limbs.
